Networkingk8s 1.35

Debugging Service Traffic

A Service exists and its name resolves, so why does the app behind it never get the call? Three links must hold: the selector matches the Pod labels, a matching Pod is Ready (unless publishNotReadyAddresses is set) so the EndpointSlice serves it, and targetPort is the port the container listens on. Break either of the first two and no endpoint is serving, while a wrong targetPort lands where nothing listens. A named targetPort follows the port the Pod declares.

▶ Play the animation 5 steps, animated, best on a wide screen

How it works, step by step

  1. The client calls web on port 80 and the name resolves to the ClusterIP 10.96.0.20. The call reaches the app only while three links hold: the selector matches the Pod labels, the Pod is Ready so the slice serves it, and targetPort 9376 is the port the container listens on.

    Play from this step

  2. The Pod carries app=web-v2 while the selector still asks for app=web. Nothing matches, so the Pod is not listed even though it is Ready, and the EndpointSlice holds no endpoints at all. The name still resolves and the client still sends, but with nothing behind the Service the call never reaches a Pod.

    Play from this step

  3. The labels match again, but the Pod is not Ready, for example because its readiness probe fails. The slice still lists it, marked not ready, so no endpoint is serving and the call never reaches a Pod, unless the Service sets publishNotReadyAddresses, which marks every endpoint ready.

    Play from this step

  4. Now the Pod is Ready and the slice serves 10.244.2.7:9376, so both empty-slice checks pass. But the container listens on 8080 while targetPort still says 9376. A numeric targetPort goes into the endpoint as it is, so the call reaches the Pod on a port where nothing listens.

    Play from this step

  5. Naming the port takes the number out of the Service. The targetPort becomes a port name, and the Pod declares containerPort 8080 under that name, so the endpoint resolves to 10.244.2.7:8080, where the container listens, and the call is served. If the port moves, only the Pod changes, and its declaration has to move with the process.

    Play from this step
